summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and gastroparesis was admitted after a syncopal episode following dialysis. The episode occurred in the setting of persistent hiccups, nausea, vomiting, and poor oral intake, leading to dehydration. The hiccups, which had improved after a prior admission, returned and were controlled with intravenous Thorazine. An echocardiogram showed preserved systolic function with moderate diastolic dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension. The syncopal event was attributed to hypovolemia rather than a cardiac or neurological cause. The patient was rehydrated, tolerated a regular diet, and completed scheduled hemodialysis. Baclofen was added to his regimen to prevent hiccup recurrence. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all medications and follow up with his primary care physician and nephrologist.
